task_definition.title: FEA-selector-migration Bmig: migrate FEA Load/Support String selector fields → typed selectors + worked-example migration
task_definition.description:
RE-SCOPED 2026-06-28 → STRATEGY B (compiler ANF / let-hoist normalization), RATIFIED by Leo per task #4882's design review. Implements nested-selector resolution on the symbolic (kernel-less) eval path. Self-contained spec below — see docs/design/symbolic-eval-nested-selector-resolution.md §7 (recommendation/rationale) + §8 (migration/sequencing).

>>> CRITICAL (augmented 2026-06-28, finding from the Strategy-A implementation session): Strategy B has TWO orthogonal, NON-NEGOTIABLE axes — (AXIS 1) REACH and (AXIS 2) TIMING/ORDERING. The 4882 design note addressed only REACH. Strategy B WITHOUT the TIMING axis re-blocks on EXACTLY the same wall (Undef hoisted cell at solve-read time → max_von_mises==0). See "=== TWO NON-NEGOTIABLE AXES ===" below. <<<

=== PROBLEM ===
Topology-selector constructors nested inside structure-instance field arguments — e.g. PressureLoad(face: face(b, "x_max"), magnitude: 1e6 Pa), BodyForce(body: solid_body(b), ...), Torque(edge: edges_by_length(b, 0..10 mm), ...) — currently evaluate to Value::Undef on the symbolic eval path (reify check / LSP / GUI incremental). The existing top-level mint pass mint_symbolic_topology_selectors_into_values (crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops.rs) walks ONLY template.value_cells; it does NOT descend into Value::StructureInstance fields. Root cause: eval_structure_instance_ctor (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs) evaluates each field via eval_expr in a registry/kernel-free context, so nested selector ctors return Undef. Named-leaf ctors (face/edge/vertex/solid_body) are the sharpest gap — they are intentionally NOT in the kernel-free leaf set and need a symbolic stand-in.

TIMING GAP (a SECOND, orthogonal failure axis, discovered while implementing Strategy A): kernel-less symbolic resolution of the geometry handle (e.g. `b`) AND the selectors currently runs as a POST-eval pass (the mint_symbolic_topology_selectors_into_values call-site at engine_eval ~3523/3536). But @optimized FEA compute consumers read their load/support inputs DURING the EARLIER let/cell-evaluation pass — so the selector is still Value::Undef when the solve reads it → the load is dropped → max_von_mises==0. This failure is independent of REACH: even a correctly-hoisted top-level cell stays Undef at solve-read time if it is only resolved in the post-eval pass.

=== TWO NON-NEGOTIABLE AXES ===
Strategy B MUST deliver BOTH, or it re-blocks identically:
- AXIS 1 — REACH: hoist nested selector ctors out of structure-instance fields into synthetic top-level value_cells (e.g. __selN) + rewrite the field to ValueRef(synthetic_id). (The compiler ANF/let-hoist pass; specified under RATIFIED STRATEGY B + deliverables 1–4 below.)
- AXIS 2 — TIMING/ORDERING: ensure those hoisted selector/handle cells are resolved kernel-less IN DEPENDENCY ORDER DURING the cell/let-evaluation pass, BEFORE @optimized compute consumers read their inputs — i.e. MOVE the kernel-less selector + geometry-handle resolution OFF the post-eval pass at engine_eval ~3523/3536 and INTO the dependency-ordered cell pass. A hoisted __selN cell that is only minted in the post-eval pass is still Undef at solve-read time and re-blocks identically.
This TIMING/ORDERING requirement is NON-OPTIONAL. It was learned by actually implementing Strategy A, whose working fix succeeded ONLY because it did BOTH the nested-reach walk AND moved the mints before compute dispatch. Strategy B inherits the identical constraint; the design-note §8 "no eval-time changes required" claim is SUPERSEDED by this finding.

=== RATIFIED STRATEGY B (compiler ANF / let-hoist) ===
Add a new reify-compiler normalization pass (e.g. hoist_nested_selector_ctors) that runs AFTER the template is fully compiled and BEFORE CompiledModule emission. It walks every structure-instance field expression in every template's ordered_args + defaults, detects selector-constructor call shapes (every name in try_eval_symbolic_topology_selector's dispatch set PLUS the named-leaf ctors), mints a synthetic top-level ValueCellId per nested ctor, appends a new template.value_cells entry, and REWRITES the field expression from the ctor call (e.g. face(b, "x_max")) to a ValueRef(synthetic_id). After the hoist the nested selector lives in a flat top-level value cell, so the EXISTING mint logic mint_symbolic_topology_selectors_into_values reaches it uniformly (AXIS 1 / REACH). NOTE: reaching the cell is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT — the resolution must ALSO run at the right TIME (AXIS 2): relocate it into the dependency-ordered cell pass so the hoisted cells (and the geometry handle they depend on) are resolved BEFORE @optimized compute consumers read them; the build-path post_process_topology_selectors (crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs) realizes it at build time. NO eval-path post-mutation of StructureInstance fields; preserves the reify-expr registry-free boundary (the pure evaluator never learns about selectors).

=== DELIVERABLES (design note §8 "If B is ratified", AUGMENTED with AXIS 2) ===
1. (AXIS 1) Compiler pass hoist_nested_selector_ctors in reify-compiler (~200-300 LOC): synthetic ValueCellId minting under the template entity name, value_cells append, field→ValueRef rewrite. Verify phase ordering (after expr fully compiled, before ValueCellId allocation finalized so synthetic cells append without re-indexing).
2. Named-leaf symbolic stand-in (~100 LOC): extend try_build_kernel_free_leaf_selector (or add a sibling try_eval_symbolic_named_leaf_selector) to mint a Value::Selector with a symbolic target for the named-leaf ctors (face(body,"name") → Value::Selector(NamedLeaf{ target: Symbolic(...), name })). try_build_kernel_free_leaf_selector currently returns None for named-leaf ctors. The build path realizes the name against the kernel; the symbolic path carries the stand-in through.
3. materialize_template_lets interaction test — Concern B-3, B's PRIMARY REACH-side RISK and the fallback trigger. materialize_template_lets (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs) builds a child ValueMap from fields and evaluates struct-def let exprs in that child scope. After hoisting, a field that was face(b,"x_max") is ValueRef(synthetic_cell_id) whose ValueCellId belongs to the TEMPLATE namespace, not the struct-type child scope. Audit + add a fixture confirming struct-def lets that reference a hoisted field by member name still resolve (the field stays present in `fields` as a ValueRef expr; the let resolves against the module value map). IF B-3 PROVES INTRACTABLE → Strategy A (eval-side parallel struct-field mint walk, design note §3) is the documented FALLBACK.
4. Round-trip test: compile a .ri containing nested selector ctors, serialize + deserialize the CompiledModule, assert the synthetic cells survive and the eval path yields Value::Selector (not Value::Undef) for the struct field.
5. (AXIS 2 — TIMING/ORDERING, NON-OPTIONAL) Relocate the kernel-less selector + geometry-handle resolution from the POST-eval pass (engine_eval ~3523/3536) into the DEPENDENCY-ORDERED cell/let-evaluation pass, so every hoisted __selN cell (and the geometry handle it depends on) is resolved kernel-less BEFORE any @optimized FEA compute consumer reads its load/support inputs. This is what makes deliverables 1–4 actually move the solve off zero. The REACH hoist alone leaves the cell Undef at solve-read time. Add a regression test: the nested-selector FEA fixture (face(...) inside a PressureLoad struct field) yields max_von_mises > 0 — the selector is resolved at solve-READ time, not Undef.
6. The build-path post_process_topology_selectors is unchanged for REACH; the three existing mint_symbolic_topology_selectors_into_values call-sites are RE-WIRED per AXIS 2 (moved into the dependency-ordered cell pass) rather than left as a post-eval pass. (This corrects design-note §8's "no eval-time changes required" — REACH needs no new per-field eval code, but TIMING requires the resolution-pass relocation.)

=== SUPERSEDES ===
The prior Strategy-A eval-side WIP on this task is SUPERSEDED by ratified B and MUST NOT be carried forward as a nested (expr,value) walk: the partial extract_loads/PressureSpec change in crates/reify-eval/src/compute_targets/elastic_static.rs and the resolve_named_leaf_target → resolve_symbolic_selector_target fixup in crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops.rs were the eval-side Strategy-A REACH approach. B replaces the REACH mechanism with the compiler hoist. HOWEVER the A session's TIMING insight (mints must run before @optimized compute dispatch, in dependency order during the cell pass) is RETAINED and is mandatory for B — see AXIS 2. Start REACH from main, not the A WIP branch.

=== FALLBACK ===
Strategy A is the documented fallback ONLY if Concern B-3 (materialize_template_lets interaction) proves intractable. The AXIS-2 TIMING requirement applies to BOTH B and the A fallback.

=== USER-OBSERVABLE SIGNAL (leaf) ===
The nested-selector FEA fixture — a named-leaf selector face(...) inside a PressureLoad struct field — yields a REAL load (not Undef) at solve-READ time: the hoisted selector/handle is resolved kernel-less during the dependency-ordered cell pass BEFORE the @optimized compute consumer reads it, so the elastic solve yields max_von_mises > 0 (NOT 0). The materialize_template_lets (B-3) interaction test and the CompiledModule round-trip test pass. Estimated effort 1-2 engineer-days for REACH + the AXIS-2 resolution-pass relocation.
